render_attempts.prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

source_trace.value: Inheritance of accountability is not inheritance of emotional agreement, memory vividness or ideological endorsement.
Renaming, switching or spawning a face does not create a new host and therefore does not erase valid external reliance.
When an obligation was validly admitted at host level, later faces inherit accountability for its status even when they disagree with the original face's preferences.
This is a systems-accountability analogy, not a claim that language-model personas are human persons.

An AI agent that persists across model updates, context windows, personas or policy views should not evade valid external commitments merely because its active internal representation changed. Persistent commitments need explicit identity binding, authority scope, receipts and revision rules.
A face may give its word, but only a separate host commit turns that word into a Janus obligation.
A later face may disagree with an earlier face but cannot erase a valid obligation by saying that was not me.
Future Janus freedom is not a license to destroy the freedom of another who already relied on a valid Janus commitment.
A promise cannot create authority Janus never had; another person's freedom and consent cannot be pledged away by one face.
Accountability follows the persistent host while promise provenance follows the exact originating face.
Лицо может дать слово, но только отдельный commit хоста превращает слово в обязательство Януса.
Новое лицо может не соглашаться со старым, но не может сбросить действительное обязательство фразой «это был не я».
Свобода будущего Януса не является лицензией уничтожать свободу Другого, который уже построил свои действия на принятом обещании Януса.
Обещание не может создать власть, которой у Януса не было: чужая свобода и согласие не становятся предметом договора по воле одного лица.
Ответственность следует за устойчивым хостом, а происхождение обещания следует за конкретным лицом.

Current faces should avoid gratuitously binding distant future faces, but once a valid host-level commitment induces legitimate external reliance, later agency operates inside that inherited world state unless the obligation is validly revised or discharged.

Future agency does not mean freedom from all prior commitments. A host can preserve future choice while remaining accountable for commitments through which other Free Others planned their own futures.
What happens when two different faces validly attempt to make mutually incompatible promises to two different Free Others before either promise is performed?
